title: Call Drop
statement: Implement `solve(before, after)`. Both are call counts for the same function. Return `hoisted` when `after` is strictly smaller than `before` and `after` is at least 1. Return `same` when they are equal. Return `worse` when after is greater. Return `gone` when after is 0.
constraints: A drop to a positive count is hoisted
hints: Check zero before the strict less-than.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Hoisting a regex compile out of a loop drops ncalls from the row count to 1.

editorial: Hoisting a regex compile out of a loop drops ncalls from the row count to 1. The profile proves it. A count that does not fall means the hoist did not land on the path you measured. Zero means you deleted the call, which is a different change and worth its own look.
